title: Lower viscosity may drive apical-out polarity reversal of airway spheroids

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Lower viscosity may drive apical-out polarity reversal of airway spheroids

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors hypothesize that airway spheroids keep cilia in the lumen because basal cells interact with the surrounding high-viscosity matrix, and that moving spheroids to a lower-viscosity, water-based medium may trigger basal cells to migrate inward so the ciliated apical layer takes their place on the spheroid surface.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Given that cilia naturally localize into the lumen due to the basal cells’ interaction with the surrounding high‐viscosity matrix, we hypothesized that changing the culture environment to a lower viscosity level (e.g., water‐based media instead of gel‐based matrix) may trigger the basal layer cells to migrate inward and allow the apical layer to take their place on the spheroid cortex.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Human Bronchial Epithelial Cells Self‐Construct into Multicellular Motile Living Architectures”. Scope: Human bronchial epithelial spheroids grown in Matrigel and transferred to low-adhesive liquid culture

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-03: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed polarity-switch mechanism makes clear temporal predictions. Existing endpoint and motility data do not contain the lineage-resolved, independently controlled measurements needed to discriminate it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Perform live lineage imaging across controlled viscosity changes and test whether basal cells move inward before apical ciliated cells occupy the cortex, relative to matched matrix controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Endpoint staining does not establish layer migration order.

Viscosity changes are confounded with adhesion, matrix chemistry, and stiffness.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.72
data existence: 0.4
data adequacy: 0.28
operationalizability: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Basal-cell position over time is a measurable variable, and the paper states the inward-migration route as a hypothesis tied to viscosity. Public material, if any, is endpoint immunostaining, which is compatible with several rearrangements. Distinguishing inward basal migration from other polarity switches needs new live imaging or a deposited tracking set that does not exist.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Live-image basal and apical markers from the moment spheroids leave Matrigel until cilia are external, and test whether basal cells move inward rather than apical cells moving outward or new cilia differentiating in place. Inward basal migration that precedes external cilia would support the viscosity hypothesis; polarity reversal without basal displacement would refute that particular route.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The cell-resolution movies that would separate the routes are not deposited.

Viscosity is changed by leaving the gel, which also changes adhesion and ligand presentation.

Endpoint stains at day 0 and day 7 do not track which cells moved.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.68
analysis feasibility: 0.22
data existence: 0.18
